title: The Story of the River Ganga
captions: After the yajna, the sages said, “King Janaka of Mithila is holding a great yajna. Come and see the mighty bow he keeps there.” So the princes set out with Vishvamitra, and in time they reached the holy river Ganga.
Rama looked at the sparkling water and asked, “Great sage, how did the Ganga come to flow on the earth?” The princes sat close to their teacher and listened carefully.

“Long ago,” said the sage, “your ancestor King Sagara of Ayodhya began a great yajna with a sacred horse. But the horse vanished! His sixty thousand sons searched the whole earth and dug deep below it.”
“At last they found the horse beside the great sage Kapila, who sat in peace. Thinking he was the thief, they rushed at him in anger. With one mighty sound, the sage turned them all to ashes.”
“Only the holy Ganga, flowing down from heaven, could bring peace to their souls. Sagara's great great grandson, King Bhagiratha, prayed for many long years, until Lord Brahma granted his wish.”
“But Ganga's fall was so mighty that it could break the earth. So Lord Shiva stood on the mountain and caught her in his matted hair. Then, at Bhagiratha's prayer, he gently let her flow out.”
“Ganga followed Bhagiratha's chariot all the way to the ashes, and her holy water set the sons of Sagara free. That is why she is also called Bhagirathi.” The princes listened in wonder.
story: After the yajna, the sages told the princes about a great yajna being held by King Janaka of Mithila, where a mighty bow was kept. So Rama and Lakshmana set out with Vishvamitra, and in time they reached the banks of the holy river Ganga.
Rama looked at the sparkling water and asked how the Ganga had come to flow on the earth. The princes sat close to their teacher, and Vishvamitra told them a story about their own family.

Long ago, King Sagara of Ayodhya began a great yajna with a sacred horse, but the horse vanished. His sixty thousand sons searched the whole earth and even dug deep below it. At last they found the horse beside the great sage Kapila. Thinking he was the thief, they rushed at him in anger, and with one mighty sound the sage turned them all to ashes.

Only the holy Ganga, flowing down from heaven, could bring peace to their souls. Kings of the family tried for generations to bring her down. At last King Bhagiratha, Sagara's great great grandson, prayed for many long years until Lord Brahma granted his wish.

But Ganga's fall was so mighty that it could break the earth. So Lord Shiva caught her in his matted hair and then gently let her flow out. Ganga followed Bhagiratha's chariot all the way to the ashes, and her water set the sons of Sagara free. That is why she is also called Bhagirathi.
lesson: When Rama asked about the river, he did not rush on. He and Lakshmana sat close to their teacher and listened with full attention, and through listening they learned the story of their own ancestors and of King Bhagiratha, who never gave up. In our tradition, Shravana, careful listening, is the first step of all learning. The wisdom of the Vedas was kept alive for thousands of years by people who listened well and remembered.
lesson_long: When Rama asked about the river, he did not hurry on. He and Lakshmana sat close to their teacher and listened with full attention. Through listening, they learned the story of their own ancestors and of King Bhagiratha, who never gave up.
Our elders teach that good listening is a kind of respect. When we truly listen, we learn more, and the person speaking feels valued.
tradition: The Vedas were kept alive for thousands of years through listening. They are called shruti, which means what is heard. Teachers chanted, and students listened and repeated until they knew every word by heart.

Even today, when someone works very hard for something that seems impossible, people call it a Bhagiratha effort. Many Hindu families keep a little Ganga jal, water from the Ganga, at home for prayers.
words: what is heard; another name for the Vedas
another name for the Ganga, after King Bhagiratha
holy water from the river Ganga
a great sage of deep wisdom
question: Who tells you stories about our family or our traditions? What is one story you remember well?
questions: Who tells you stories about our family or our traditions? What is one story you remember well?

What makes it easy or hard for you to listen carefully?
card_lesson: Rama and Lakshmana sat close to their teacher and listened with full attention. Shravana means listening carefully, so that what we hear can become wisdom in our hearts.
